audit.whatIsWrong: Content win[] gave Mel all 7 stages (packet chart too, flagged as a defect vs 46.4% WR) while the full layer read Mel/Mel/Mel/Skill/Skill/Kassadin/Kassadin — the two layers disagreed on rows 4-7.
audit.why: Mel dominates pre-6 (Kassadin has no ranged trade tool); Kassadin's scaling — Rod of Ages, scaling Q shield, Riftwalk dropping toward 2s — flips the last two stages. Full layer's shape is right; its Skill rows 4-5 were moved to Mel to match the content whys that describe Mel denial and a first-spike level 6.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 Mel on both layers, rows 6-7 (First item, 2+ items) Kassadin on both layers, whys rewritten to match.

audit.why: Spikes real: Mel pre-6 poke window and Luden's before his Rod of Ages; Kassadin 6 (Riftwalk), Rod of Ages, and the 2-3s R at max rank late.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digits; Q's magic-damage-absorbing shield and W auto-reset burst tell were unmentioned; spikes[3] called his Q a silence, which it has not been for years (Riot text: interrupts channels); enemyWin was a name-swap template.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s; Q 9s with a magic shield that eats Mel's burst — force it out first; only Q is a projectile, so Rebuttal reflects nothing else in his kit; W is an auto reset (burst tell).
audit.corrected: Cooldowns rewritten with 5s/2s/9s/38s; reflect limits written into dontsFull[2].d; Q-silence claim removed from spikes[3]; enemyWin grounded in survive-to-6 scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: The missing-interactions file claims Solar Snare cancels Null Sphere as a channel, but the channel flag contradicts Riot's own text — Q INTERRUPTS channels, it is not one.
audit.why: Derived-flag misfire per the calibration guidance; not written to the page.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to 6, then Riftwalking past your snare and cashing Rod of Ages scaling before you end.

edits.before: Luden's spike: snare-volley chunks half bars and the execute cleans the remainder. Force contacts.
edits.after: His Rod of Ages finishes and the Q shield starts eating your volleys — the all-in threat is his now.

edits.before: First item lands well before his Rod of Ages, so your lead only widens.
edits.after: Rod of Ages done, his shielded all-in beats your poke; play for picks.

edits.before: Late Mel is a counter-artillery battery: reflect their poke, snare their dive, and execute the chipped.
edits.after: Two-plus items his Riftwalk is a 2-3s blink with real burst — he stat-checks you; fight only with peel.

edits.before: At two items you're still ahead of his scaling curve if you've pressed the early advantage.
edits.after: At two-plus items his Riftwalk falls to 2-3s and the stat check is his; never walk alone.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Rebuttal like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Kassadin Riftwalk (R): 5s at rank 1, 2s at max — post-6 the lane runs on its timer. - His Q shield (9s) absorbs magic burst; force it out before you commit. - Guard your 38s Rebuttal like a fifth summoner spell.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: The glow forces him to open with Null Sphere into the reflect or hold his combo — either way you bought a free step and a free volley.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Riftwalk, his W auto and Force Pulse all ignore Rebuttal — only Null Sphere reflects, so the glow buys less here than against mages.

edits.before: This is where Kassadin wants to be, so your job is to have ended the game already. If it goes long, save Rebuttal for his Q-silence engage and use Golden Eclipse to reset fights, but never get caught alone where he can R-chain onto you.
edits.after: This is where Kassadin wants to be, so your job is to have ended the game already. If it goes long, save Rebuttal to reflect his Null Sphere opener and use Golden Eclipse to reset fights, but never get caught alone where he can R-chain onto you.

notes: Chart resolved to Mel rows 1-5 / Kassadin rows 6-7 on both layers; packet's Mel 7/7 chart was self-flagged as contradicting the 46.4% WR. The _missing file's 'Null Sphere is a channel your Snare cancels' is a derived-flag misfire (Riot text says Q interrupts channels) and was deliberately not written. spikes[3] 'Q-silence' corrected — Null Sphere no longer silences. W auto-reset burst tell noted in audit but no natural field had room within the length band; recorded here rather than forced in. Ratings left unchanged.
